summary: Whatcom Co., WA 20-ft treated timber tower with R-6 cab, built 1962 on Dillard Point; removed or destroyed in 1981, with footings and an outhouse still reported on site.

facts.design: 20-foot treated timber tower with an R-6 flat cab
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1981 per the register, FireLookout.com, WillhiteWeb and Washington Lookouts. WillhiteWeb reports footings, an outhouse, and wiring and posts on the site; the site is said to be completely grown over.

access.note: Reached over Baker Lake Road and forest roads 12 and 13, then a 0.7-mile walk along an old road. WillhiteWeb notes one major washout and says the road may have been abandoned for good. No closure is recorded in the sources, and the road account dates to about 2014.

visit.trail_note: Park where an old road leaves FR 13, then follow the old road 0.7 miles to a large opening with a high gravel embankment; the lookout is just above it.

events.note: June 29, 1961 Marysville Globe item: a lookout house and tower to be constructed in the Baker River drainage. Quoted by Washington Lookouts; the register and FireLookout.com date the build to 1962.
20-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, per the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb.
Removed per the register and Washington Lookouts. FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1981.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A June 1961 newspaper item, quoted by Washington Lookouts, announced the tower. The register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb date it to 1962. The story gives both dates.
The register and Washington Lookouts say the tower was removed in 1981. FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1981. The story reports both words.
The register and FireLookout.com give 2,400 feet, which matches the brief's 731.5 m. WillhiteWeb gives 2,360 feet. The story says about 2,400 feet.

notes_for_editor: No staffing record was found in any of the four sources, so staffing is left out. The 1961 newspaper item is known only through Washington Lookouts; the newspaper itself was not checked. The road and site account is about 2014 at the latest, so current conditions are unknown. Build year (1961 item vs 1962) and removal wording (removed vs destroyed) both conflict across sources. Brief record matches the register on tower type, elevation and agency.
